question: Why did the union take 3 h 48 in STUDIO-R57 and R58 against 2 h 03 in R52 and R54, and what are the largest cuts to round time that keep proof?

answer.status: PARTLY_PROVEN: where the time went is measured; why the machine state changed is UNVERIFIED
measured: Builds, not tests. R54 to R57 grew 6290 s: build +4987 s (79%), first test listing +638 s (10%), test run +450 s (7%), doctests +179 s (3%). R52 to R58 grew 6308 s: build +4713 s (75%), first listing +897 s (14%), test run +485 s (8%), doctests +155 s (2%).

The work did not grow in step. Same rustc 1.97.1 and nextest config; per-unit compile counts are nearly identical for common units. Workspace Rust lines rose 4.1% R52 to R58 and harness test lines 3.4%, while build time rose 82%. R57 and R58 differ by 9 changed paths and took the same time.

Compute was not the limit. Long CPU-bound develop tests stayed flat (R56 to R58 sum ratio 1.11, median per test 0.98) while some short tests jumped from under a second to 8-10 s. Whole-machine CPU mean stayed 16-17% in R56, R57, R58; disk queue mean (all disks summed) rose from 13.1 to 18.9 and 19.7, and in build phases from 15.9 to 21.6.

A machine-state signature exists. The validator's C: tree walk took 2-27 s in R52, R54 and R56 at all times; in R55, R57 and R58 the longest walk inside each heavy build was 181-1144 s, while walks between heavy builds stayed near 6 s. 37 of 51 long walks in R57 and R58 ended within 60 s of a heavy unit's build end.

The disk lock played no part. Waits per round were 1-10 s in total, 1 s at most; all gaps between units were 7-29 s per round. No builder took a C: gap, and no GPU lock wait line exists in any run log of the five rounds.

why_91_units_equalled_160.answer: MEASURED. Unit count barely moves time: R57's 68 extra units cost 795 s (small nextest and doctest units), while the heavy harness family and the default unit, present in both rounds, are 77-81% of each. R58's common units ran 776 s slower than R57's, which cancelled the 795 s. R52 and R54 show the same equality when the machine was healthy: R54's 67 extra units cost 602 s.

unverified: The cause of the slow state. No memory, commit or per-disk reading exists inside any round; the first commit reading is 18:05Z, 93 minutes after R58 ended.

How much the 44 watchers, Chrome, the tree walk and the full C: disk each contributed. Watchers and the fuller disk arrived between R56 and R57; when Chrome grew is not recorded; watchers and Chrome's size were both gone before R59, so R59 cannot separate them.
Compile versus link inside a build: logs carry only cargo's total per unit, and the C: round target was off limits.
That the first listing's extra cost is Defender scanning new executables.

method.timestamps: File mtimes in results/Rxx. build start = empty build.stdout.txt; build end = build.stderr.txt (within about 15 s of cargo's Finished time); run start = empty run.stdout.txt; run end = run.stderr.txt. Doctest wall = its stdout/stderr end minus previous unit end. Test execution = nextest Summary line. Lock = disk-lock.json.
method.first_list: The gap between build end and run start. Source-verified at cargo-nextest 0.9.148 (registry copy, src/dispatch/core/run.rs): exec_run builds the binary list (line 1045), then build_test_list executes every test binary with --list, and only then returns because no_run made runner_builder None (lines 245-247, 1139). So `--no-run` also runs every freshly linked binary once. Attributing the whole gap to that listing is inference; nothing else runs there per the code and run-round.sh.
method.second_list: Run wall minus nextest Summary: cargo's fresh check plus the second listing.
method.load: load-poll.log (typeperf single 1 s samples about every 62-86 s, R56-R58 only; disk queue is PhysicalDisk(_Total), summing 7 disks). No memory counter is recorded in any round.
method.tree_walk: csize.jsonl of the validator cap guard, robocopy /L over C:/HandshakeBuild/WP-KERNEL-STUDIO and again per child.
method.not_read: R59 results, the C: round target, refund-claim-20261021.md. No cargo, build, test or process control.

stalls.definition: test time at least 5 s over its minimum across R52, R54, R56, R57, R58
stalls.periodicity: Cluster start seconds spread evenly over the minute and gaps show no 60 s period, so no watcher tick is visible. Clusters sit inside each harness unit's run.

test_level.duplication: R58 ran 5600 test instances of 2773 distinct tests; R57 8813 of 4960.

disk_lock_and_builders.verdict: MEASURED: the 300 s slice cost nothing visible. 15-21 yields per round, waits 1-10 s total, gaps between units 7-29 s total. A builder consuming a gap would have shown as a long wait; none did.
disk_lock_and_builders.note: HANDOFF calls R57's 28 m default build outside load. The validator's own probe builds on D: overlapped it (07:30-08:33Z), and R56's 13 m comparator also had a probe. R52 had two D: builders during its default build and still took 11 m 18, so D: builds alone do not explain it; effect UNVERIFIED.

suspects.name: Builder holding the C: disk lock
suspects.evidence: waited_s_total 1-10 s in all five rounds.

suspects.name: Code or unit growth
suspects.evidence: +4.1% lines against +82% build; R57 to R58 almost no code change; R58 has fewer units.

suspects.name: 44 leftover watchers of the lead
suspects.evidence_against: Started 2026-11-06T02:30Z at the earliest, yet R51, R53 and R55 were slow before that (heavy10 448, 598, 533 s against 355 s in R54). Machine CPU mean did not rise (17.3, 16.9, 16.2%). No 60 s period in test stalls.
suspects.evidence_for: Timing fits R57 and R58. Mean CPU held while the round took 60% longer, so total CPU-seconds rose about 50% (47k to 71k core-s, derived from samples): about 1.7 extra cores for 3.8 h, source not identified. Each lane_watch tick forks git, python and ls per lane.
suspects.ledger: Commit free 3.9 GB right after stopping them, so they were not the memory shortage.

suspects.name: Chrome memory shortage
suspects.evidence_against: No reading during R57 or R58: readings 6.4, 9.3, 8.5 GB are at 18:05, 18:48, 19:40Z, after R58 ended at 16:32Z. No os error 1455 or paging-file text in R57 or R58 logs. Page file PeakUsage since boot reads 15.3 GB today (whether a resize resets it: UNVERIFIED), so heavy page-out is not shown. Chrome's size in R51, R53, R55 is unknown.
suspects.evidence_for: CPU was unsaturated while jobs slowed and disk queue rose, which fits a starved file cache. Chrome process count 478-484 in R57 and R58 df-log, but that is count, not memory.

suspects.name: Cap guard tree walk (new suspect, validator-side)
suspects.evidence: Busy 92-100% of R57 and R58, 69% of R55, 30% of R51, 3.5-6% of R52, R54, R56. Its script samples every 60 s from 250 GiB instead of 120 s, and the tree passed 250 GiB only in R57 and R58 (296-314 GiB; team-dev 21 to 102-115 GiB). Each sample walks the tree twice. Its walks stall only in slow rounds, so it is at least a symptom. Counterexample: R53 was slow with walks at a median 4 s.

suspects.name: C: disk full (Samsung 870 QVO 8 TB, SATA; QLC per the model line, not checked here)
suspects.evidence: Free fell from 414-456 GB (R52, R54, R56) to 228-251 GB (R57, R58, 97% used); drive model read today. R55 was slow at 420 GB and R56 fast at 430 GB, so free space alone does not decide it.

suspects.name: Time of day (correlation only)
suspects.evidence: Starts at 04:40-05:44Z (R51, R53, R55) were slow, 10:47-11:49Z (R52, R54, R56) faster, 20:47Z (R50) fastest; R58 at 12:44Z breaks the pattern.

suspects.name: GPU contention
suspects.evidence: GPU utilisation mean 35% in R55 and R56, 1.3-1.7% in R57 and R58; builds are the growth.

cuts.note: Hours per round. Not additive. Healthy basis R54 (2:03), slow basis R58 (3:48). Cuts 2 and 4 are commits to checked-in config: CX-VAL-007 applies, CX-VAL-011 forces a full round, and R54 shows a canary when a root input changes (R54-canary took 1:57), so each costs about 4-6 h once. Cut 3 is a product test change through a lane. Cuts 1 and 5 touch no checked-in round config.

ranked.cut: Keep rounds out of the slow state
ranked.how: Dispatch-level, no commit: read R59 against the index below; add commit, available memory, cache and per-disk queue to the validator's load poll; replace the cap guard's double tree walk with C: free delta or a far slower cadence; start validator probes after the default unit builds.
ranked.proof_risk: None for the union. The cap guard must still stop the round before 355 GiB; free delta can miss bytes others write, so keep one real walk at start and end.
ranked.next_measure: R59 has Chrome at 14.1 GB and no watchers but five D: builders. heavy10 near 355-470 s and walks under 20 s would show the state gone, without separating the causes.

ranked.cut: Drop 5 harness feature units whose features are strict subsets of retained ones: viewer, media, media-native, audio-device, audio-batch
ranked.kind: MEASURED unit wall; effect on later rounds assumes other units unchanged
ranked.how: Commit to .config/round-features.toml, retain desktop+viewer, studio-aac, os-encode, audio-plugin, audio-batch+audio-device. Feature closure read from harness Cargo.toml: every dropped set is implied by a retained one. The only tests that gain proof under specific features (studio-aac AAC 5.1, desktop AccessKit) stay.
ranked.proof_risk: Exact sets stop being built: code that compiles or passes only with those exact sets goes unseen, such as a missing import when media is on and audio-batch off. Further candidate with the same trade: harness-view+viewer (0 exclusive tests; 134 s R54, 364 s R58). 40 cfg(not(feature)) sites exist in harness and harness-view (desktop 16, audio-batch 12, media 6); negative branches still run in retained units that lack that feature, but not in those exact combinations. Mitigation, at extra cost: cargo check --tests per dropped set, cost UNVERIFIED.

ranked.cut: Merge harness's 74 integration test targets into one test binary
ranked.kind: ESTIMATED (40-70% of heavy build and first list; link share not measured)
ranked.evidence: Measured: 10 viewer-family units compile only 2-5 crates (one with 29) yet take 315-409 s in R54, while light units with the same 74 targets, mostly empty without viewer, take 29-58 s. 54-71 of 74 binaries hold tests; each is compiled, linked and listed per unit.
ranked.how: Product change through a lane: tests/ becomes one crate with modules; same for harness-view (33), render-gpu (36), composite (59) later. First measure compile versus link once with cargo --timings outside a round.
ranked.proof_risk: Nextest still gives each test its own process, so semantics hold. Test ids change their binary name, so claim mappings and validator history must migrate; one file failing to compile fails all tests in that unit.

ranked.cut: Raise .cargo/config.toml jobs from 8 to about 16 for rounds
ranked.evidence: Measured: CPU mean 14-16% of 32 threads in build phases, about 5 cores with 8 slots. No load data for R54 itself. If disks are the limit, the gain shrinks.
ranked.proof_risk: No proof change. Risk is a failed round: os error 1455 at 32 jobs on 2026-10-24 and a builder failure at 5.4 GB commit free. Needs the commit gate kept and machine-wide builders counted, since the file also serves lanes.

ranked.cut: Windows Defender and Search exclusions for C:/HandshakeBuild and the artifact root
ranked.kind: ESTIMATED; measured floor if scanning is the cause: first list exceeds second list by 0.13 h (R54) to 0.35 h (R58)
ranked.evidence: Measured today: real-time protection on, tamper protection on, Search service running, exclusion list unreadable without admin. HANDOFF records no exclusions. First listing costs 4-6 times the second over the same binaries.
ranked.proof_risk: No proof risk. It is a security trade-off and an Operator setting; the lead only reports it.

smaller_measured.cut: Skip doctest units with zero doctests
smaller_measured.evidence: R54 84 of 103 units, R58 46 of 55 units have none; they build the lib and find nothing.
smaller_measured.proof_risk: Loses the doc-build compile check for that set; a new doctest must re-enter the plan mechanically.

smaller_measured.proof_risk: The cold first-run cost moves into the run step; build and run stay separate records.
